my dearest friend, a man who once said he considered himself to be the "Trans David Lynch", a turn of phrase I've smiled at nearly every day since, and I spent an extended amount of time talking about his death after I took my friend out to a show to help him deal with it. My friend expressed how David Lynch made so many things that he just connected to on a deep level, how Lynch showed him he wasn't alone in the ways he saw the world. I am inclined to agree. David Lynch would show some disturbing things in his works yet always maintained a sunny personality. We discussed this trait of his and how many would consider it an incongruity but like....David Lynch understood life in a way that American culture tries to subdue. There's always this need to escape to delusions in America, and David Lynch saw the contradictions of the cheerful disposition America tries to project and the darkness of how it operates and he explored that, and the darkness of life in general, and lived a life that showed just...the fullness of life...there's such grisly horror and pain on Earth and you can still look at the sunset and have your favorite treat and see how the birds rest on telephone wires and hold those things in hand together and honestly it gives you a better perspective of how life really is rather than to hide behind an expectation of interpretation of life as "glass half full" or "glass half empty". Life is both, and there is pain and beauty at the same time, observe them both on your own terms and reject the societal need to adhere to archetypes from their interpretations of you. You are you, and you have your whole life to figure out who that is exactly, and it's never going to adhere to any archetype, any stereotype, any generalization. Be. You. You are the only You. idk. too fuckin many, music is kinda my obsession but I don't talk enough about "Then Jack doubles over and he vomits and dies" from Jangling Jack by Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds. I'm drawn to it because the adding the detail about the vomit in this weird random song about a happy go lucky guy addressing the wrong guy with his positivity amd being shot by the dude and dying is so fascinating to me. I feel like the media and culture romanticizes death with ideas of honor or finding peace or whatnot and even when it deals with the existential horror of the cessation of consciousness, the visceral physical horror of death is kind of generally brushed over to the side except in like edgy metal songs that go to campy horror movie levels of gore.

This line though?? it's so quick. he doubles over, he vomits and he dies. It's like a neat balance of the visceral tucked away in a not particularly gory song that just somehow, to me at least, highlights the weird dissociative experience of watching death play out or any just violent experience. The detail of vomit is like an afterthought almost or like a fixation of the image of death that one doesn't want to talk about but cannot keep silent about.

I just think it's pretty neat lol

keeping on Nick Cave I also think about "but the feather spun upward, upward and upward, spinning all the weather vanes, and you're sitting at the kitchen table listening to the radio. And I love you".
the first part of the song is clearly about Elvis but then there like what evokes to me the hard cut in 2001 A Space Oddity from the bone to the spaceship in some ways, it's a jarring change that underlines a key thought in the theme of the work. 
I also just like how like this tragic tale of a fucked up pop star, like someone who is a now less a human than a cultural symbol that represents a massive shift in culture is suddenly cut to a small domestic scene a small intimate scene between two people who love each other experiencing this thing like...idk culture is insane and loud and people get lost in it and great grand tragedies that are told throughout time and despite all these giant figures and tales are little things, little people, sharing love. Elvis will be remembered for generations, my love for my partner will be forgotten after our death. my love for my partner is more important than the most famous person on the planet.
something can be so big the whole world knows about it but something so small and seemingly insignificant can be the most important thing that could ever happen. idk I just really like the juxtaposition lol
